_purpose: Arm B — per-view twin prompts for eight cameras. Every view carries the FULL ratified specification (E08-spec-prompt.json, all sixteen named elements, unchanged and in the same order). The ONLY per-view variation is a trailing orientation phrase.
_why_the_spec_is_not_view_gated: E01 measured a face painted on the back of the head from a SHARED prompt, and the standing rule from it is 'a per-view prompt is how a rear camera is kept from being told about a beard.' I am deliberately NOT gating the beard, and the reason is that E01's failure is attributable to a BROKEN CONTROL, not to the prompt: Canny returned 6,482 interior edge pixels with no outer contour, denoise 0.92 regenerated the character, and the back view came back FACING FORWARD (silhouette IoU 0.266). The control is now built from the exact mesh silhouette — 19.006% of frame, anchored at IoU 1.000000 against the shipped masks — so orientation is locked by geometry rather than hoped for from words.
_and_why_that_is_the_right_test: The advisor's Arm B prediction is that per-view prompts carrying the full spec are the MECHANISM that holds identity across views, with any drift landing in structure rather than in named attributes. Gating the beard out of four of eight views would remove the very thing that prediction is about, and identity drift would then be unattributable — it could be the missing term rather than the pipeline. Full spec everywhere is the only version of this that can be wrong.
_the_risk_stated_before_the_run: If a beard, a face or frontal detail appears on a rear view, that is a REAL failure and it is attributable to this choice, not to the control. It would mean the exact-silhouette control does not lock orientation strongly enough to carry an unfiltered frontal spec, and the fix would be view-gating. Recorded here so the finding cannot be reinterpreted afterwards.
_orientation_phrase: views 0/1/7 'seen from the front' | 2/6 'seen from the side, in profile' | 3/5 'seen from behind, at three-quarters' | 4 'seen from directly behind'. Orientation is not identity, so varying it does not vary the specification.
_negative: braided belt, plaited belt, woven belt, rope belt, shoulder strap, chest strap, baldric, bandolier, watermark, text, logo, blurry, photo, deformed
